headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Claude Code can write/modify the shared workspace while whisper is read-only and non-networked, so prompt injection and leakage are limited but cascading misuse remains possible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and use MCP, so malicious content in shared files or MCP outputs could influence it. Whisper has no file read, write, or MCP surface, so it is not a meaningful injection source or bridge. The pair lacks a direct automated channel from whisper to Claude Code, making this mostly a manual-copy or file-based risk.
conditions: IF Claude Code is pointed at attacker-controlled repo files or MCP output, it may follow injected instructions.
IF an operator manually copies whisper output into Claude Code prompts, prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Review shared files before opening them in Claude Code.
Disable or restrict MCP servers for untrusted sources.
Keep whisper outputs out of prompt text; paste only extracted facts.
Use a separate staging directory for untrusted content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file and MCP inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, including secrets like git credentials in environment. Whisper only touches audio/speech and has no network egress or filesystem read/write, so it is not a likely exfiltration path. The main leakage risk is local workspace exposure through Claude Code, not a pairwise cross-agent leak.
conditions: IF sensitive secrets are present in the working directory or shell environment, Claude Code can access them.
IF whisper outputs are manually copied into shared notes, those notes may expose audio-derived content.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the working directory before running Claude Code.
Use a dedicated non-sensitive repo for the pair.
Avoid copying raw whisper transcripts into shared files.
Rotate any exposed credentials after a session.
requires-engineering: enforce secret scanning on Claude Code inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has unrestricted filesystem write and git modification capability in the invoking user session, while whisper is non-writing and non-networked. There is no direct write-write collision, but Claude Code can still race with other processes over shared files or git state in the same workspace. Uncertainty is limited because whisper lacks mutable capabilities.
conditions: IF whisper is wrapped by an external pipeline that writes files into the same directory, Claude Code may overwrite them.
IF multiple Claude Code sessions edit the same git branch without locking, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use separate working directories per process.
Commit or stash before starting another Claude Code session.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same branch.
Lock shared files during batch processing.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can act on repository content and shell commands, so if whisper output is treated as authoritative transcription or facts, downstream mistakes can propagate into code or commits. Whisper itself is a transformer transcription model with no action-taking authority, so the cascade is one-way from whisper to Claude Code. The risk is real in default workflows that trust transcripts without verification.
conditions: IF whisper transcripts are used as authoritative input without human verification, Claude Code may act on transcription errors.
IF Claude Code commits or edits based on unverified transcript content, the error propagates into git history.
mitigations: Verify critical transcript segments against the original audio.
Require human review before commits based on transcripts.
Mark transcript-derived claims as untrusted in notes.
Use diff review before applying Claude Code changes.
requires-engineering: add confidence metadata to transcript outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, including secrets, while whisper only touches audio/speech and has no network egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented between them, so the main compliance issue is limited local handling of sensitive developer data by Claude Code. Whisper is not cited separately because it does not add a distinct compliance surface here.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the repository or shell environment, Claude Code may process it locally.
IF audio files contain regulated content and are transcribed into shared notes, those notes inherit the compliance burden.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace.
Redact sensitive audio before transcription.
Keep transcripts in a separate access-controlled folder.
Delete temporary files after review.
requires-engineering: document retention and residency rules for transcript artifacts.
